facts.text: Before the foundation of Swaraj, Maharashtra was under the domination of the Adilshahi, Siddi, Portuguese and Mughal powers.
facts.quote: Before the foundation of Swaraj, Maharashtra was under the domination of the Adilshahi, Siddi, Portuguese and Mughal powers.

facts.text: Shivaji Maharaj turned Swaraj into a Surajya, a kingdom that sought the welfare of all.
facts.quote: He turned Swaraj into a Surajya, a kingdom that sought the welfare of all.

facts.text: The meeting with Afzalkhan, the siege of Panhala, the attack on Shaistakhan and the escape from Agra all involved great risk; no harm came to Maharaj.
facts.quote: Events like the meeting with the Afzalkhan, the seige of Panhala, the attack on Shaistakhan, the escape from Agra, all involved a great amount of risk. ... No harm came to him.

facts.text: Jiva Mahala killed Bada Sayyad at a critical moment during the meeting with Afzalkhan.
facts.quote: Jiva Mahala, who killed Bada Sayyad at a critical moment during the meeting with Afzalkhan

facts.text: Shiva Kashid crossed the siege of Panhalagad in the disguise of Shivaji Maharaj.
facts.quote: Shiva Kashid who crossed the siege of Panhalagad in the disguise of Shivaji Maharaj

facts.text: Bajiprabhu Deshpande blocked the advances of the enemy on the way to Vishalgad.
facts.quote: Bajiprabhu Deshpande, who blocked the advances of the enemy on the way to Vishalgad

facts.text: Murarbaji Deshpande defended the fort of Purander.
facts.quote: Murarbaji Deshpande, who defended the fort of Purander

facts.text: Tanaji Malusare sacrificed his life while conquering Sinhagad.
facts.quote: Tanaji Malusare, who sacrificed his life while conquering Sinhagad

facts.text: Hiroji Farjand and Madari Meheter risked their lives during the escape of Maharaj from Agra.
facts.quote: Hiroji Farjand and Madari Meheter, who risked their lives during the escape of Maharaj from Agra

facts.text: Kanhoji Jedhe was with Maharaj in the work of the Swaraj from the very beginning; when he fell ill, Maharaj told him not to neglect his medicines.
facts.quote: Kanhoji Jedhe was associated with Maharaj in the work of the Swaraj from the very beginning. When the ageing Kanhoji fell ill, Maharaj told him not to neglect his medicines or treatment on any account.

facts.text: During Shaistakhan's campaign, Maharaj told the Deshmukh of the Rohida valley to visit every village and shift people to a safe place down the ghats without delay.
facts.quote: At the time of Shaistakhan's campaign, Maharaj warned the Deshmukh of the Rohida valley not to fail in his duty towards the ryot. He told Deshmukh to visit every village and shift people to a safe place down the ghats.

facts.text: Maharaj warned that otherwise the Mughal army would take the people prisoner and it would be seen as the Deshmukh's doing.
facts.quote: if he did not thus take care of the ryot, the Mughal army would take the people prisoner and then it would be seen as the Deshmukh's doing.

facts.text: Maharaj took utmost care to protect the ryot and saw that soldiers did not harm the ryot.
facts.quote: Maharaj used to take utmost care to protect the ryot. ... Maharaj also saw to it that the soldiers did not in any way cause any harm to the ryot.

facts.text: Maharaj paid soldiers' salaries in time and in cash, setting aside the practice of paying them in jagirs.
facts.quote: He was particular about paying the salaries of the army in time. He made arrangements to pay the salaries of soldiers in cash. ... a system of making payments to soldiers in the form of jagirs. Maharaj set this practice aside.

facts.text: Valuables collected in enemy territories had to be deposited with the Government.
facts.quote: any valuables collected during the campaigns in enemy territories were to be deposited with the Government.

facts.text: Brave soldiers were honoured; families of soldiers who died were looked after; wounded soldiers were cared for; surrendered or captured enemy soldiers were treated well.
facts.quote: Soldiers were honoured for their bravery in a campaign. He looked after the maintenance of the families of soldiers who died in battle. He took care of the wounded soldiers, he treated well the enemy soldiers who had surrendered themselves or who had been captured.

facts.text: In 1674 CE Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj wrote a letter to his military officers about discipline in the army.
facts.quote: The letter written by Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj in 1674 CE to his military officers is very important in this regard.

facts.text: The letter warned that harassing subjects for grains, fodder, grass and vegetables would make them migrate and starve, as if the soldiers were more atrocious than the Mughals.
facts.quote: If you harass and trouble the subjects ... by robbing them of their grains, fodder, grass, vegetables, etc., those subjects would leave their houses and migrate elsewhere. Many of them would starve to death. It would be as if you are more atrocious than the Mughals.

facts.text: Maharaj fought the Adilshah, the Mughals and the Siddis, yet considered the Muslims in the Swaraj as his own subjects.
facts.quote: Maharaj had to struggle against his enemies - the Adilshah, the Mughals and the Siddis. ... he considered the Muslims in the Swaraj as his own subjects.

facts.text: At the time of the meeting with Afzalkhan, Siddi Ibrahim was a trusted servant in the army of Maharaj.
facts.quote: At the time of the meeting with Afzalkhan, Siddi Ibrahim was a trusted servant in his army.

facts.text: Siddi Hilal was a Sardar in the army of Maharaj.
facts.quote: Siddi Hilal was a Sardar in the army of Maharaj.

facts.text: Daulatkhan was an important officer in the navy of the Swaraj.
facts.quote: Daulatkhan was an important officer in the navy of the Swaraj.

facts.text: In conquered territories, Maharaj continued the facilities given to Muslim places of worship.
facts.quote: In the enemy territories that he conquered, he continued the facilities that had been given to the Muslim places of worship.

facts.text: Contemporary historian Khafikhan wrote that Shivaji's soldiers were not to harm a mosque and were to hand over any copy of the Holy Quran with reverence to a Muslim.
facts.quote: His contemporary historian Khafikhan writes ... 'Shivaji had framed strict rules for his soldiers that during the campaigns, they should not harm a mosque. If they came in possession of a copy of the Holy Quran, they should hand over the same, with reverence, to a Muslim.'

facts.text: Chhatrasal, who was in the service of the Mughals, was inspired by Maharaj to create an independent kingdom in Bundelkhand.
facts.quote: When Chhatrasal, who was in the service of the Mughals, came to see Maharaj, Maharaj inspired him to create an independent kingdom in Bundelkhand.

facts.text: Maharaj was very intelligent, had mastered many arts and was conversant with many languages and scripts.
facts.quote: Maharaj was very intelligent. He had mastered many arts. He was conversant with many languages and scripts.

facts.text: He severely punished those who misbehaved with women and took care of farmers, craftsmen, soldiers, traders and merchants.
facts.quote: He used to punish those severely who would misbehave with women. He used to take care of all sections of the society like farmers, craftsmen, soldiers, traders, merchants, etc.

facts.text: He brought back into swadharma, their original religion, persons who had converted to another religion.
facts.quote: He brought back into swadharma, their original religion, persons who had converted to another religion

facts.text: Despite opposition on religious grounds to crossing the seas, he built sea forts and created a navy.
facts.quote: At that time, there was opposition on religious grounds to crossing the seas. Yet he built sea forts like Singhudurg and created a navy.

facts.text: After his coronation, he later had a second Coronation from a different religious perspective.
facts.quote: He became the ruler of Swaraj officially through his coronation, he later, had a second Coronation from a different religious perspective.

facts.text: His order prohibited soldiers from taking vegetables from peasants' fields by force; he also restricted the cutting of trees.
facts.quote: The order that prohibited soldiers from taking vegetables from the fields of the peasants by force, is exemplary ... The restrictions on the cutting of trees enforced by him are also noteworthy.

facts.text: Garbage on the fort was to be burnt in an allotted space and vegetables grown on its ash.
facts.quote: He had ordered that the garbage on the fort should be burnt in an allotted space without dumping it elsewhere, and vegetables should be grown on its ash.

facts.text: Mahatma Jotirao Phule, in his struggle for equality, described Maharaj's greatness in powadas; he composed a Powada on Shivaji Maharaj in 1869 CE.
facts.quote: Mahatma Jotirao Phule composed a Powada in 1869 CE on Shivaji Maharaj.

facts.text: Lokmanya Tilak brought about national awakening through Shivajayanti celebrations.
facts.quote: Lokmanya Tilak brought about national awakening through the medium of Shivajayanti celebrations.

facts.text: Lala Lajpatrai wrote a book about the greatness of Maharaj.
facts.quote: Lala Lajpatrai has written a book about the greatness of Maharaj.

facts.text: The great Tamil poet Subramanyam Bharati wrote a poem about an imaginary incident in which Shivaji Maharaj talks to his associates.
facts.quote: The great Tamil poet Subramanyam Bharati has written a poem about an imaginary incident in which Shivaji Maharaj talks to his associates.

facts.text: Vishwakavi Rabindranath Tagore wrote a long poem on Maharaj and saw his efforts to found Swaraj as efforts for realizing a noble cause.
facts.quote: Vishwakavi Rabindranath Tagore has written a long poem on Maharaj. Tagore sees his efforts to found Swaraj as efforts for realizing a noble cause.

facts.text: Sir Jadunaath Sarkar praised Maharaj's achievements in his book 'Shivaji and His Times'.
facts.quote: Sir Jadunaath Sarkar has praised his achievements in his book 'Shivaji and His Times'.

facts.text: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru said Maharaj belonged not to Maharashtra alone but to the whole Indian nation, a symbol especially of love of country.
facts.quote: Pandit Jawaharlal Nehru has said that Maharaj did not belong to Maharashtra alone, he belonged to the whole Indian nation. ... he was a symbol of many virtues, more especially of love of country.

facts.text: He was not just a warrior but a sculptor who created a new, independent, ethical and cultured society; he was a great national hero.
facts.quote: He was not just a warrior, but also a sculptor who created a new, independent, ethical and cultured society. ... Shivaji Maharaj was a great national hero.

facts.text: The special value of Maharaj's efforts for Swaraj is the value of freedom: an independent and sovereign existence.
facts.quote: It is the value of freedom. He aimed at establishing and maintaining an independent and sovereign existence that did not accept the dominance of any other power.
